extracted.intended_audience: general encyclopedia readers, students, researchers interested in medical associations, policy, and history
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of the American Medical Association covering its history, governance, published standards and codes, policy positions, and influential programs (e.g., CPT, specialty/residency standards, ethics). Useful for readers wanting a summary of AMA's organizational rules, standards, and policy stances.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization maintains the AMA Code of Medical Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the Association's authoritative set of ethical principles for physicians (mentioned as an organizational standard; no further details on specific provisions provided on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: AMA Physician Masterfile
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMA Physician Masterfile containing data on United States Physicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A data standard/system that establishes a file for each physician when an individual either enters medical school or enters the United States; used to track graduates and practicing physicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician Specialty Codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Physician Specialty Codes — the standard method in the U.S. for identifying physician and practice specialties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published by the AMA as a standard taxonomy for classifying physician specialties and practice types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) coding system
rubrics_metrics.description: The Current Procedural Terminology coding system was first published in 1966 and is maintained by the Association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Created for uniform reporting of outpatient physician services; first manual had 4‑digit codes and 163 pages, with later editions expanding (e.g., adding a fifth digit in 1970). It is an AMA-maintained clinical coding standard used in billing and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guides to the Evaluation of Permanent Impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMA has published works such as the Guides to Evaluation of Permanent Impairment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Guides are published reference standards for assessing permanent impairment; the page notes editions and committee review processes for revisions (e.g., initial 1971 publication, later editions and committee reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for medical specialty training / residency programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMA established standards for medical specialty training residency programs and published lists of hospitals approved for residency training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically the AMA created and published standards and approval lists (Council on Medical Education and Hospitals published annual lists of hospitals approved for internships in 1914; standards for specialty training published in the 1920s). These function as accreditation/approval benchmarks for residency/internship programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital approval / internship lists (standards for training sites)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMA's Council on Medical Education and Hospitals published its annual list of hospitals approved for internships in 1914 and later published lists of hospitals approved for residency training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published lists acted as an approval standard for which hospitals met AMA criteria to host internships/residencies; used historically to guide medical education placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME) certification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal partnership between the AMA and the Association of American Medical Colleges formed the Liaison Committee on Medical Education in 1942 in order to establish requirements for certification of medical schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LCME sets standards and requirements for medical school accreditation/certification in the U.S.; the AMA's role in forming the LCME indicates participation in establishing those educational standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council on Pharmacy and Chemistry standards and voluntary drug approval program
rubrics_metrics.description: AMA created the Council on Pharmacy and Chemistry in 1905 to set standards for drug manufacturing and advertising; that year the AMA began a voluntary program of drug approval which required drug companies to show proof of the effectiveness of their drugs to advertise them in AMA's journal (program remained in effect until 1955).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents AMA-set quality and advertising standards for pharmaceuticals historically, including a voluntary pre-advertising effectiveness requirement enforced via AMA publication policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: House of Delegates and board of trustees governance model
rubrics_metrics.description: The American Medical Association is governed by a House of Delegates as well as a board of trustees in addition to executive management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: House of Delegates modeled after the U.S. House of Representatives and includes representatives from medical organizations across the U.S.; functions as the Association's central legislative/policy-making body — a procedural governance standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician Masterfile enrollment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Physician Masterfile is established when an individual either enters medical schools or enters the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the procedural trigger/criterion for creating an AMA Masterfile record for an individual physician.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMA policy position: opposition to government-run health insurance / single-payer
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically the AMA has lobbied against various forms of government-run health insurance; the AMA is opposed to single-payer health care and at its 2019 House of Delegates meeting voted to maintain its opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes institutional policy stances that guide AMA advocacy and lobbying: historically campaigned against compulsory or government-backed insurance, framed such proposals as 'socialized medicine', and currently opposes single-payer systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMA advocacy to restrict physician supply (policy/actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: At various points the AMA advocated for restricting the supply of physicians (e.g., lobbying to close substandard medical schools, capping Medicare reimbursement to hospital residency positions, limiting foreign-trained doctors' entry and training slots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These policy actions reflect an institutional stance and advocacy strategy that affected physician workforce numbers; the page documents legislative/lobbying tactics and historical outcomes (e.g., long-term effects on physician shortages).

rubrics_metrics.name: AMA stance on scope-of-practice (opposition to expansion without physician oversight)
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization has lobbied against allowing physician assistants and other health care providers to perform basic forms of health care and, in modern times, has opposed 'scope of practice creep' where non-physicians provide services without physician oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents AMA policy that shapes advocacy, social media campaigns, and interactions with allied professional organizations; the page notes controversies and pushback from physician assistant and nurse practitioner groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance use and addiction policy positions
rubrics_metrics.description: AMA positions have included calling alcoholism an illness (1956), launching a 'war on smoking' (1972), supporting legislation to prohibit tobacco sample disbursement and advertising bans, proposing higher drinking ages, and creating the AMA Opioid Task Force (2014) to evaluate opioid use/abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are public health policy stances and programmatic responses that guide AMA advocacy, clinical guidance, and public messaging on substance use and addiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical malpractice reform policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMA has supported changes in medical malpractice law to limit damage awards (caps on pain-and-suffering damages) as a policy to influence malpractice litigation and physicians' practice locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legislative/policy criterion the AMA advocates for to affect liability environment and healthcare market behavior; the page cites examples and mixed evidence on effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positions on LGBTQ+ rights and gender-affirming care
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMA supports allowing transgender and intersex athletes to compete in sports that align with their gender identity; supports allowing trans people to use single-sex facilities aligning with their gender identity; supports public and private insurance coverage for gender-affirming care; and has issued statements advocating for puberty blockers for transgender youth and opposing restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bundle of policy positions defines AMA guidance and advocacy concerning LGBTQ+ health: clinical support for gender-affirming care, opposition to legislative/administrative restrictions, and public statements/letters opposing CMS and other rules that would limit access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancing Health Equity: language, narrative and concept guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMA published 'Advancing Health Equity: A Guide to Language, Narrative and Concepts' asking questions about language and commonly used phrases and offering equity-based, equity-explicit, and person-first alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a communication/style guideline intended to cultivate awareness about dominant narratives and to recommend language choices to improve health equity and address structural racism in healthcare discourse.
